items.title: Correctional officer from Mississauga, 21, posed as OPP cop in Toronto park, claim police
items.summary: According to police, the suspect approached a vehicle in a park parking lot, identified himself as an Ontario Provincial Police officer and displayed a metal badge. A Mississauga man, 21, has been charged with personating a peace officer and breach of trust by public officer. A correctional officer from Mississauga has been charged after police say he posed as a provincial police officer in a Toronto park. m. on Nov. 22 after a “suspicious incident” was reported in the parking lot, say Toronto police. According to police, the suspect approached a vehicle in the park parking lot, identified himself as an Ontario Provincial Police officer and displayed a metal badge. The suspect then demanded identification from the people in the vehicle and ordered them to leave the vehicle, say police. Officers located a suspect nearby and arrested him. A 21-year-old man has been charged with personating a peace officer and breach of trust by public officer.

items.title: Plans for new youth hub ‘at risk’ in Mississauga, mayor says
items.summary: 6-million youth hub planned for Mississauga’s east end is “at risk” of delay or not being built at all due to unexpected recent developments, the mayor says. In the advanced stages of planning and “only weeks away from receiving a full building permit,” the Glenforest Youth Hub project is now on hold pending further agreement between the City of Mississauga and the Peel District School Board, Mississauga Mayor Alvin Tedjo and Ward 3 Coun. Chris Fonseca said in a letter to provincial Education Minister Paul Calandra. In the letter, dated Nov. 23, Tedjo and Fonseca noted that a recent appraisal of the hub site at Glenforest Secondary School has somewhat altered the financials of the agreement. ” It also “builds upon the successful model established through the Malton Youth Hub,” a facility that’s enjoyed success since opening in late 2023. “Unfortunately, the (Glenforest) project is now at risk,” Tedjo and Fonseca continued in their letter. “The city has already invested approximately $3 million in design and development work and is only weeks away from receiving a full building permit. ” Rendering shows what the exterior of the Glenforest Youth Hub will look like. Mississauga said it remains committed to working with the education ministry, the school board and other stakeholders “to identify a mutually beneficial solution.

items.title: Video: ‘Assault-style’ firearm seized after Mississauga break-in and crash
items.summary: Two 18-year-old men were charged after a break-in and crash in Mississauga where officers seized an “assault-style” firearm, Peel police say. The incident happened on Feb. 18, 2025, following reports of a break-in, Peel Regional Police tell INSAUGA Canada. Investigators say four suspects broke into a home, and a resident called police to give officers a description of a vehicle. A short time later, police say they were contacted about a crash involving the same suspect vehicle at Glen Erin Drive and the Collegeway in Mississauga. A video shared by police shows officers arriving at the crash scene, where the vehicle suffered severe front-end damage and came to a stop in a snowbank. A break-and-enter investigation by our Central Robbery Bureau led to the recovery of an assault-style firearm and the arrest of a suspect. Officers responded to a home invasion and break-and-enter involving suspects armed with assault-style rifles. Shortly after the incident, the suspects carjacked a victim at gunpoint, stole the victim’s vehicle.

items.title: Why is Mississauga mayor proposing consolidation of advisory committees?
items.summary: The Region says it will contribute $5 million to the project… Mayor Alvin Tedjo pledges affordability, economic growth and… If approved, each consolidated committee will reduce resident representation to six community members and two council members. Mississauga Mayor Alvin Tedjo waved and thanked the people in the audience at the inaugural ceremony. He’s bringing a proposal to his first council meeting as mayor to consolidate several advisory committees. Mississauga’s new mayor is proposing an overhaul of several city advisory committees — a move that some residents say could curtail opportunities for public input on muncipal decision-making. The motion, by Mayor Alvin Tedjo, is coming to the first council meeting of the new term on Nov. ” The motion proposes three new advisory committees: According to the motion, the proposed committees will include two council members and six citizen or business members with expertise in each committee’s area of focus. Once appointed, the existing advisory committees will be retired.

items.title: Cop who fatally shot Mississauga man offers condolences to family at inquest
items.summary: Last Updated November 24, 2026 at 6:44 pm A police officer who shot a Black man in the head during an attempted arrest in Mississauga nearly seven years ago told a coroner’s inquest Tuesday that he did not make a conscious decision to open fire but instead acted out of a “fight-or-flight” instinct. Peel regional police Const. Milan Ivkovic was part of a team of plainclothes officers in unmarked vehicles who sought to arrest Jamal Francique near his home on the evening of Jan. 7, 2020, over an alleged breach of bail conditions. The inquest has heard officers planned to arrest Francique before he got to his car, but he moved more quickly than expected, and the officer meant to block his car was late. Francique reversed out of his parking spot and briefly came to a stop, Ivkovic testified. Meanwhile, an unmarked police car pulled up, putting its nose to the vehicle’s bumper, he said. Ivkovic got out of his car and walked toward Francique’s vehicle, which was still stationary, he said. In that time, another unmarked police car came up behind Francique’s car, and the officer could hear people shouting commands, he said. As he stepped up onto the curb, Ivkovic saw Francique’s car suddenly reverse and lurch forward, accelerating toward him, he said. The officer said he fired his gun four times “in the area of where a driver would be,” though he couldn’t see a figure inside. Under cross-examination, a lawyer representing Francique’s father suggested Ivkovic should have known it was “prudent” to move out of the car’s way.

items.title: Massive holiday celebration returns this weekend to Port Credit in Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga’s village by the lake will be lit up with festive colours with Light Up the Port 2026, a free family event. Happening this Saturday, November 28 from 4 pm to 9 pm, this beloved annual event is a festive evening of fun, holiday entertainment, music, shopping and plenty of Christmas cheer for the whole family. This year the festival will include a brand new interactive experience: visitors can check out six towering, illuminated musical structures that come alive with light and sound when stepped on, in partnership with Visit Mississauga. It all happens at Port Credit Memorial Park. Many events and activities are lined up for this year’s celebration: Annual Christmas Tree Lighting: The lighting of the Port Credit Christmas tree happens at 6 pm, officially welcoming the start of the holiday season. Lighting of the Port Credit Lighthouse: The lakeside village’s iconic lighthouse will be lit up in beautiful colours. Free Family Photos with Santa: Capture a special holiday memory with jolly old St. Nick at no cost. PC Polar Express: Hop on for a trackless train ride inspired by the beloved Christmas film.

items.title: Mississauga Pauses Large-Scale Data Centre Development While It Studies Planning Rules
items.summary: According to city officials, Mississauga has temporarily paused approval of new large-scale data centre development while it studies how future projects should be planned and managed. The city says it is inviting community members to learn about its data centre policy review and get involved, as the rapid growth of artificial intelligence drives rising demand for data centres across North America. Data centres are being proposed and built in many towns and cities across the continent to support that growth, officials noted. Cities cannot automatically stop development from happening, but they can set rules for how it occurs, officials said. The review will draw on input from partner agencies, other levels of government and members of the public, according to the city's notice to residents.

items.title: Slim Third-Ballot Win Makes Navdeep Bains the New Ontario Liberal Leader
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, former Mississauga and Brampton MP Navdeep Bains has won the Ontario Liberal Party leadership, prevailing by a narrow margin in a third round of voting on Nov. 21. The party says more than 20,500 members cast ballots, a 15 per cent increase in turnout from the previous leadership race. Bains spent years moving between federal politics, teaching and the private sector before entering the provincial race. In a statement following the result, Bains said he was honoured by the trust Ontario Liberals placed in him and declared the party ready for what he called Ontario's moment.

items.title: Mississauga's Election Sign Ban Faces Charter Challenge As Rights Group Intervenes
items.summary: According to the Canadian Constitution Foundation, the group has been granted leave to intervene in a court challenge against the City of Mississauga's total ban on election signs on public property. The case was brought by longtime political candidate Greg Vezina, whose campaign signs were removed from public property under the city's by-law in 2019. Vezina argues the by-law is a content-based restriction, since the city allows other signs, such as those advertising housing developments and farmers' markets, while banning only election signs. His application will proceed to a hearing at the Superior Court of Justice over whether the ban violates free expression under the Charter. CCF interim litigation director Josh Dehaas said sign bans disadvantage lesser known candidates, since signs are one of the few affordable ways to reach voters against established politicians.

items.title: Toronto Police Say Mississauga Man Used Fake Badge to Pose as Officer at Etobicoke Park
items.summary: According to Toronto Police, a Mississauga man employed as a correctional officer at the Toronto South Detention Centre is accused of posing as a police officer during an encounter at Colonel Sam Smith Park in Etobicoke this past Sunday. Police say the man approached occupants of a vehicle in the parking lot, identified himself as an Ontario Provincial Police officer and displayed a metal badge. He then demanded identification from the occupants and directed them to exit the vehicle, according to police. Responding officers located a suspect near the scene shortly afterward, police said in a news release. Joshia Jiju Koshy, 21, of Mississauga, was arrested and charged, and is scheduled to appear at the Ontario Court of Justice in Toronto on Feb. 16, 2027.

items.title: Mississauga Budget Committee Set to Weigh MiWay Fare Hike This Week
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga's budget committee will consider a proposal this week to raise MiWay transit fares starting Jan. 1, 2027. Senior city staff are recommending the increase to help offset rising costs tied to inflation, labour, maintenance and service delivery, according to a report set for Wednesday's meeting. The report notes MiWay still faces a revenue shortfall despite previous fare adjustments. Sam Rogers, the city's commissioner of transportation and works, said in the report that the proposed changes reflect a balanced approach to current revenue and ridership realities. City councillors are expected to debate the recommendation before any fare changes take effect.
